portanigra.name: Porta Nigra
portanigra.slogan: Rome's grey gate, still guarding Trier's front door.
portanigra.line: A Greek monk named Simeon lived as a hermit in its ruins from 1028, and the gate was turned into two churches.

dom.name: Trier Cathedral
dom.slogan: A Roman core under eight centuries of Gothic stone.
dom.line: Its core from around 340 makes it the oldest church building in Germany still in use.

konstantinbasilika.name: Basilica of Constantine
konstantinbasilika.slogan: An emperor's throne hall, bare brick and 33 metres of air.
konstantinbasilika.line: Built around AD 300-310, this 67-metre hall is the largest surviving single room from classical antiquity.

saarschleifecloef.name: Saarschleife at the Cloef
saarschleifecloef.slogan: The Saar doubles back on itself, and you watch from above.
saarschleifecloef.line: The river runs about 10 km around the bend, yet Besseringen and Mettlach are only 2 km apart as the crow flies.

bernkastelmarkt.name: Bernkastel Market Square
bernkastelmarkt.slogan: Timber gables and a house as narrow as a wine bottle.
bernkastelmarkt.line: The Spitzhäuschen, the narrow Pointed House on the market square, dates from 1416.
